title: Optimal Combinations of Broadly Neutralizing Antibodies for Prevention and Treatment of HIV-1 Clade C Infection
sections_or_artifacts_inspected: Methods/Results lines 280-307; Figs. 1-2; Data Availability; local S1 supplement DOCX and extracted table inventory
evidence_and_overlap: 15 bnAbs/200 acute or early viruses for single-agent susceptibility. Ten combinations were assayed on a selected 20-virus subset chosen to be sensitive to almost all bnAbs and maximize IC80 range. Fig. 2 compares measured combo outcomes and Bliss-Hill predictions. The 1,622 combination scores over 200 viruses are predictions, not measured combo outcomes.
access_level_and_limit: Full primary article and local supplement DOCX inspected; local extraction has a 21-row x 7-column summary coverage table, not an isolate-level raw table. Fig. 2 exposes measured points; row-level values/group IDs not reconstructed.

title: Predicting neutralization susceptibility to combination HIV-1 monoclonal broadly neutralizing antibody regimens
sections_or_artifacts_inspected: Methods, sample-size simulations, Fig. 4 caption, Data Availability; author repo README and get_catnap_data.sh
evidence_and_overlap: Observed CATNAP susceptibility is individual-bnAb IC50/IC80. Combination IC50/IC80 values are calculated from single-agent measurements under additive/Bliss-Hill models (Fig. 4 caption), not measured combination assay outcomes. The paper evaluates held-out pseudovirus susceptibility prediction and synthetic sample-size performance, not measured combo decision stability.
access_level_and_limit: Primary paper and public author-repository metadata/README inspected. One targeted data-folder fetch was blocked by the browser access layer; no raw CATNAP data downloaded. This does not make the known public individual-antibody source unavailable.

title: Design of an optimal combination therapy with broadly neutralizing antibodies to suppress HIV-1
sections_or_artifacts_inspected: LaMont et al. 2022, genetic-susceptibility and clinical-rebound model/therapy-ranking results
evidence_and_overlap: Closest clinical decision-model comparator: uses viral genetic diversity/escape and models rebound distributions to rank bnAb cocktails. It does not provide independent measured combination-neutralization rows; predicted rebound/ranks are model-derived.
access_level_and_limit: Primary article and existing public author-repository sources checked; existing HDF5 has patient trace inputs with fitted/model-derived rebound calculations, not a combo-neutralization cohort.

title: HIVTreatmentOptimization author repository
sections_or_artifacts_inspected: README, H5Output/readme.txt, JuliaScripts/file_access.jl lines 69-85 and 124-136; local hiv_trial_combo.h5 provenance/schema
evidence_and_overlap: H5 contains per-patient genetic day/site inputs and viraemic trace pairs plus fitted x/k and growth/decay values. file_access derives t_rebound=-log(x)/growth from x and uses genetic theta in simulations/rankings. access_level_and_limit: Repository says HDF5 files are processed/intermediate/final outputs (Mathematica) and posteriors/simulations run in Julia. Local file has 7 genetic IDs and 7 matching viraemic patient records; trace groups contain 10-19 pairs, no assay-level combo IC50/IC80 rows.
